llm_findings: Single causal change: cast only each Block's direct MLP-input norm result to BF16. The train.py-only plan includes necessary toggle, checkpoint persistence and logging plumbing without changing optimizer, schedule, data or evaluation.

Authoritative train.py supports the mechanism: Block.forward's FP32 lambda/residual operations precede self.mlp(norm(x)); norm() preserves input dtype when USE_BF16_NORM_OUTPUT=False; Linear.forward selects weights matching its input dtype; MLP.forward propagates that dtype through the default up/activation/down path.

The revised plan explicitly covers serial, sandwich and parallel paths without casting the shared attention input. Its coalesced-path limitation is accurate: MLP.forward uses supplied fc instead of c_fc(x), so casting the direct argument is inert for the ordinary coalesced MLP. That limitation is documented and does not affect the default candidate.

Repository evidence motivates, but does not prove, the hypothesis: the SDPA-only full run achieved 2233 steps / 1.002028 versus 2076 / 1.005967; global BF16 norm output achieved 2716 / 1.016279 versus 2071 / 1.005734. Attribution of the global regression specifically to head precision or epoch replay remains unproven.

The supplied decision log and ledger do not close the MLP-input-only experiment. This is distinct from global norm-output precision, generic FP8 autocast and previously closed MLP architecture changes. README permits this numerical-format edit; no pretrained weights, external data or evaluator modification is proposed.

The expected fixed-budget BPB improvement and throughput gain are falsifiable against the controller-pinned seed-42 same-host full-chip control. Implementation prerequisites are static inspection only; executable quality, compilation and causality checks remain smoke gates. This passes the bounded proposal review, not the exact patch or hardware authorization.
